sights.w: One of Singapore's oldest houses: a 1902 single-storey tropical bungalow built for Alexander Cashin and named for his mother Josephine Matilda — the Cashins being the Eurasian family whose patriarch became Singapore's first Eurasian millionaire. Conserved by URA in Feb 2000 and restored (façade and interior) as the clubhouse of the 'A Treasure Trove' condominium in 2015; view from Punggol Walk.
sights.k: Conserved 1902 bungalow; condo clubhouse — exterior view only

sights.address: Punggol Waterway (Sentul Crescent / Punggol Central), Punggol, Singapore
sights.w: The 4.2-km park along Singapore's longest man-made waterway, in four themed zones (Nature Cove, Recreation Zone, Heritage Zone on Old Punggol Road, Green Gallery) linked by five photogenic bridges — the dome-shaped Jewel Bridge for sunsets over the Punggol and Serangoon reservoirs, the snaking red Sunrise Bridge at the eastern Sunrise Gateway, plus the Wave, Adventure and Kelong bridges. Otters are regulars.
sights.k: Free; best at sunrise (east) and sunset (Jewel Bridge, west)

sights.w: NLB's five-storey regional library in the One Punggol hub (opened in stages Jan-Apr 2023), built as an inclusive library with interactive exhibits, tech zones and a free MakeIT maker space for 3D printing, digital cutting and robotics.
